body:
## Connections

Related to #9818 (`[meta] GPU memory allocation issues`).

## Description

Currently, `Device::new` unconditionally allocates `default_external_texture_params_buffer` (a GPU-only uniform buffer), and `Device::late_init_resources_with_queue` unconditionally creates a `StagingBuffer` (`CpuToGpu`, `MemoryFlags::TRANSIENT`) to upload its default `ExternalTextureParams` — even when the adapter does not support `Features::EXTERNAL_TEXTURE` or the application never binds a `TextureView` to a `BindingType::ExternalTexture` slot.

Because `gpu-allocator` retains the last general block of each memory type, that single 256-byte staging upload during `request_device()` permanently pins an entire host memory heap before the application creates any resources:
- **64 MiB** on DX12 with `MemoryHints::Performance` (or **16 MiB** if paired with a DX12 transient pool such as #11130),
- **16 MiB** on Vulkan with `MemoryHints::Performance` (consuming host-visible / PCIe BAR space on idle or GPU-only devices),
- **4 MiB** on DX12 and Vulkan with `MemoryHints::MemoryUsage`.

`Device::default_external_texture_params_buffer` has only a single consumer (`Device::create_external_texture_binding_from_view`).

This PR changes `Device::default_external_texture_params_buffer` from `ManuallyDrop<Box<dyn hal::DynBuffer>>` to `OnceCell<Box<dyn hal::DynBuffer>>` and creates/initializes it lazily on first use:
- In `Device::create_bind_group_inner`, pre-initializes the buffer **before** acquiring `snatchable_lock.read()` whenever any entry pairs `BindingResource::TextureView` with `BindingType::ExternalTexture`.
- In `Device::get_or_init_default_external_texture_params_buffer`:
  - Fast-path `OnceCell::get()` returns immediately once initialized.
  - Upgrades `self.get_queue()` **outside** `OnceCell::get_or_try_init` so a concurrent last-reference `Queue::drop` (which acquires `snatchable_lock` and fires user callbacks) cannot deadlock or re-enter `OnceCell`.
  - Uses `if let Some(queue) = queue.as_ref()` so calling `create_bind_group` after dropping `Queue` does not panic or allocate a staging buffer (matching `Device::create_buffer_inner`).
  - Routes `self.raw.create_buffer` errors through `self.handle_hal_error(e)` and guards `params_buffer` with `ScopeGuard` so OOM in `StagingBuffer::new` cleans up without leaking.
  - Calls `pending_writes.activate()` (necessary once `PendingWrites` has been flushed by an earlier submission) and transitions `BufferUses::empty()` -> `COPY_DST` -> `UNIFORM` (matching `zero_buffer` in `Queue::new`).
- In `Device::drop`, destroys the buffer only if `self.default_external_texture_params_buffer.take()` is `Some`.

## Isolated A/B Measurements

- **Environment**: Windows 11 (`Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26300.10075]`), Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, Intel Arc Integrated GPU (UMA, DX12 driver `31.0.101.5328`, Vulkan), `rustc 1.100.0`, `--release`.
- **Isolation & Methodology**: Unmodified `trunk` (`60cef2be`) vs this PR (`793698d8`) **alone**, both using unmodified `gpu-allocator 0.28.0` (no `#11130` or `gpu-allocator#323` applied). Strictly sequential, alternating single-process runs, `N=5` trials per cell; medians and `(min–max)` ranges reported.
- **Reproducible harness & raw data**: [`simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/wgpu-mem-bench`](https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/wgpu-mem-bench) | [`results/wgpu-11129/summary.md`](https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/blob/main/results/wgpu-11129/summary.md) | [`raw/` (100 JSONs)](https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/results/wgpu-11129/raw)

| Backend / Hint / Workload (Stage) | Baseline Allocator (MiB) | #11129 Allocator (MiB) | Δ Allocator / DXGI Local | Baseline PrivWS (MiB) | #11129 PrivWS (MiB) | Δ PrivWS | Δ Commit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DX12 `Performance` `idle` (`@dev`) | 192.0 `[128, 64]` | **128.0** `[128]` | **-64.0 / -64.0 MiB** | 267.9 (267.7–268.5) | **204.0** (203.8–204.3) | **-63.9 MiB** | **-64.3 MiB** |
| DX12 `Performance` `multi_surface` (`@peak`, 3 swapchains) | 192.0 `[128, 64]` | **128.0** `[128]` | **-64.0 / -60.5 MiB** | 269.4 (269.2–269.6) | **210.0** (209.7–210.0) | **-59.4 MiB** | **-59.4 MiB** |
| DX12 `MemoryUsage` `idle` (`@dev`) | 12.0 `[8, 4]` | **8.0** `[8]` | **-4.0 / -4.0 MiB** | 87.0 (86.8–87.1) | **83.0** (82.7–83.2) | **-4.0 MiB** | **-4.5 MiB** |
| Vulkan `Performance` `idle` (`@dev`) | 144.0 `[128, 16]` | **128.0** `[128]` | **-16.0 / -16.0 MiB** | 139.5 (138.7–155.3) | **138.5** (138.5–139.2) | -1.0 MiB | **-16.1 MiB** |
| Vulkan `Performance` `multi_surface` (`@peak`, 3 swapchains) | 144.0 `[128, 16]` | **128.0** `[128]` | **-16.0 / -15.9 MiB** | 177.8 (177.7–178.0) | **167.3** (167.3–167.6) | **-10.4 MiB** | **-10.5 MiB** |
| Vulkan `MemoryUsage` `idle` (`@dev`) | 12.0 `[8, 4]` | **8.0** `[8]` | **-4.0 / -4.0 MiB** | 18.8 (18.6–19.6) | **18.5** (18.5–18.6) | -0.2 MiB | **-4.0 MiB** |
| DX12 `Performance` `small_gui` (`@dev` -> `@peak` control) | 192.0 -> 192.0 | **128.0** -> 192.0 | **-64.0** -> +0.0 MiB | 267.8 -> 270.5 | **203.9** -> 270.4 | **-63.8** -> -0.1 MiB | **-63.4** -> +0.2 MiB |
| Vulkan `Performance` `small_gui` (`@dev` -> `@peak` control) | 144.0 -> 144.0 | **128.0** -> 144.0 | **-16.0** -> +0.0 MiB | 138.7 -> 161.5 | 138.5 -> 161.5 | -0.1 -> +0.0 MiB | **-16.1** -> +0.1 MiB |

- **Notes on metrics**:
  - On Vulkan `idle`, the full `16 MiB` / `4 MiB` reduction appears immediately in allocator-reserved memory, DXGI Local Usage, and OS Process Commit, while `PrivWS` only changes by `~0.2–1.0 MiB` because untouched pages in the Vulkan host allocation are not faulted into the working set until written; under `multi_surface` peak, Vulkan `PrivWS` drops `-10.4 MiB`.
  - Median `request_device()` latency on DX12 `Performance` `idle` improved from `82.1 ms (69.4–245.4)` to `67.9 ms (64.9–181.9)` (`68.8 -> 60.2 ms` on `multi_surface`).
  - As expected, `small_gui` (which performs its own `queue.write_buffer` / `queue.write_texture` uploads) matches baseline once the app allocates its own staging buffer.
- **Hardware/platform limitations**: Local benchmarks were measured on an Intel Arc integrated (UMA) GPU on Windows 11 and are not extrapolated to discrete GPUs (separate VRAM vs PCIe BAR/ReBAR pools) or non-Intel drivers.

## Testing

- Added two permanent automated regression tests:
  1. `tests/tests/wgpu-validation/api/external_texture.rs` (`external_texture_binding_texture_view_after_queue_drop`): verifies binding a `TextureView` to `BindingType::ExternalTexture` after `drop(queue)` succeeds without panicking (runs on `Device::noop` across all platforms/Miri).
  2. `tests/tests/wgpu-gpu/external_texture/mod.rs` (`EXTERNAL_TEXTURE_DEFAULT_PARAMS_LAZY_INIT`): verifies via `generate_allocator_report()` that neither `default external texture params` nor an eager `Staging` buffer is allocated before first use, flushes `PendingWrites` (`queue.submit([])`), runs 4 concurrent threads calling `create_bind_group` with `TextureView` -> `ExternalTexture`, verifies exact sampled GPU pixels via `get_samples`, and confirms `default external texture params` is allocated afterward.
- Verified locally on Windows 11 (Intel Arc iGPU, DX12 & Vulkan):
  - `cargo fmt --check -p wgpu-core -p wgpu-test`: pass
  - `cargo clippy -p wgpu-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` & `cargo clippy -p wgpu-test --test wgpu-gpu --test wgpu-validation -- -D warnings`: pass
  - `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg wgpu_validate_locks" cargo test -p wgpu-core --lib`: 66/66 pass
  - Standalone lock-validated (`--cfg wgpu_validate_locks`) DX12 + Vulkan hardware verification of concurrent post-flush lazy init and `drop(queue)`: pass.

## Squash or Rebase?

Single commit; ready to rebase onto `trunk`.

## LLM Use?

An AI coding agent investigated the idle device memory allocation, implemented this change and its regression tests, ran an independent concurrency/lock-order review, executed the isolated local benchmarks, and wrote this PR description under explicit contributor authorization.
